decisions.detail: QUOTE: Default: `#define MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(member) private_##member`. A field `foo` is spelled `private_foo`... With `MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS` defined: `#define MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(member) member`, so the real name is used. | WHY: The answer states both the default rename to private_<member> and the unchanged member name when MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS is defined.

decisions.mark: explains that the two branches give different consumers different views — code that defines MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS sees plain member names while an ordinary consumer of the public headers sees the renamed ones
decisions.detail: QUOTE: Default: `#define MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(member) private_##member`. A field `foo` is spelled `private_foo`, so `ctx.foo` fails to compile. ... With `MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS` defined: `#define MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(member) member`, so the real name is used. | WHY: The answer states that defining MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS gives plain member names while the default (ordinary consumers) gives the renamed `private_` names.

decisions.mark: concludes that this enforces API opacity at COMPILE time by breaking the member name, rather than by hiding the struct layout — the fields remain visible and sized
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "`#define MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(member) private_##member`. A field `foo` is spelled `private_foo`, so `ctx.foo` fails to compile. Application code that touches a field directly breaks at build time" and "the rename is the only thing that changes between the two modes." | WHY: The answer says enforcement is a compile-time break of the member name, and that the rename is the only change, so the field declarations stay in the struct. It never contrasts this with hiding the layout, so that half of the item is implied rather than stated.

decisions.detail: QUOTE: `programs/ssl/ssl_client2.c:8` and **`programs/ssl/ssl_server2.c:8`** define it at the top of the file, so these sample programs read and write SSL context fields by name. | WHY: The answer identifies that sample programs (ssl_client2/ssl_server2) define MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS themselves to access private fields directly, which is the item's substance.
